quest.title: A Novel Idea
quest.description: Chang the Ninth has made up his mind to write a new novel again, but he doesn't know where to start. He desperately needs to find inspiration...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Epic battles.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Battles, eh... Battles... There's something to that idea. It's attention-grabbing, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Though I can hardly find inspiration on that topic in Qingce Village... No battles here, let alone the epic variety...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I'd need to look further afield... In the wild! Yes, that'd do it! I hear there are many adventurers out in the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: They go roaming all over the place looking for treasure, and always end up in battle with monsters.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: As it happens, I know a place where there are plenty of monsters. Not your average monsters either, these ones are quite something! Yes! We can go there and wait for an adventurer to show up, and then witness the ensuing battle firsthand.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: And then... Haha, then I'd have everything I need! Right then! Without further ado, I shall be off! There's quite some distance to cover, so don't be too long yourselves, either!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A gushy romance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Heart and soul.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Oh, come on. Don't give me that nonsense! I'm asking a serious question here!

talks.objective: Listen in on Zhihua and Qiming's conversation

dialogues.speaker: Zhihua
dialogues.text: Hello there, Qiming! Today, I—

dialogues.speaker: Qiming
dialogues.text: Today's not good for me.

dialogues.speaker: Zhihua
dialogues.text: ...But I hadn't even said what it was yet.

dialogues.speaker: Qiming
dialogues.text: No need. I have a fairly good idea of where you were headed. And today is just not good for me.

dialogues.speaker: Zhihua
dialogues.text: Well then... when is a good day for you? Or don't you—

dialogues.speaker: Qiming
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry. The day will come. It will be a very good day for me when it does.

dialogues.speaker: Zhihua
dialogues.text: ...That tells me nothing! Qiming, please. Hear me out, now—

dialogues.speaker: Qiming
dialogues.text: Thank you, next!

dialogues.speaker: Zhihua
dialogues.text: But I haven't finished! And... what do you mean, "next"!? There isn't even a queue!

talks.objective: Listen in on Sisi and Chaoxi's conversation

dialogues.speaker: Sisi
dialogues.text: Chaoxi, you're back! I just found out how to cook this amazing new dish. Why not come back with me? I'll cook it for you!

dialogues.speaker: Chaoxi
dialogues.text: Sisi, I literally just got back and I'm completely drained, mentally and physically. I just need to lie down right now...

dialogues.speaker: Sisi
dialogues.text: Yes, of course — all that hard work, you must be exhausted. Definitely get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Sisi
dialogues.text: So... Let's have a proper catch-up after you've fully recovered, shall we? We could always set a date now...

dialogues.speaker: Chaoxi
dialogues.text: Sure, sounds great. I'll let you know. I just can't commit to a specific date right now... I'm not trying to get out of it, I just don't want to make a promise I can't keep...

dialogues.speaker: Chaoxi
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm a sailor, Sisi. And as a sailor, I'm married to the sea. You deserve much better...

dialogues.speaker: Sisi
dialogues.text: Don't talk like that, Chaoxi... You know I understand...

talks.objective: Listen in on the conversation between Little Meng, Little Fei, and Little Lulu

dialogues.speaker: Little Meng
dialogues.text: Lulu, it's definitely Fei's turn to be the captain this time.

dialogues.speaker: Little Fei
dialogues.text: Right! I keep saying, why do I have to be the first mate all the time?

dialogues.speaker: Little Lulu
dialogues.text: I just think it's more fun for everyone involved when Meng is the captain.

dialogues.speaker: Little Meng
dialogues.text: That's a bit unfair, Lulu. I think Fei plays it very well.

dialogues.speaker: Little Lulu
dialogues.text: Everyone plays their parts very well. You as the captain, me as the rich merchant, and Fei as first mate.

dialogues.speaker: Little Lulu
dialogues.text: And this time is gonna be the funnest of all! What do you think, Fei?

dialogues.speaker: Little Meng
dialogues.text: Lulu, come on...

dialogues.speaker: Little Fei
dialogues.text: Well... If that's what you think, Lulu... I—I guess it's okay by me.

dialogues.speaker: Little Meng
dialogues.text: Fei...! We've talked about this...

dialogues.speaker: Little Fei
dialogues.text: No, it's fine. I don't mind. Whatever makes Lulu happy. Come on, let's play.

dialogues.speaker: Little Fei
dialogues.text: Captain shmaptain. Not like I care.

dialogues.speaker: Little Meng
dialogues.text: ...Ugh, you guys are unbelievable...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Last time I went into the city, I saw a man talking to a young lady who appeared to be a fortune-teller. He was prattling away... I didn't bother to listen in.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I later found out the garrulous gent's name is Zhihua, and the fortune-telling lady's is Qiming. Seems there's some history there... Why don't you go ask them about their stories? If it's anything interesting, come back and fill me in.

talks.objective: Report back to Chang the Ninth

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Well, how'd it go? Got a story for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here are our notes.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Great! Let me see... Zhihua and Qiming! I knew it...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm... Yes... This is great material! Excellent!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Seriously?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Can't you see? Maybe it isn't obvious at first, but if you look closely, there's a subtle but powerful tension here... There's clearly something going on between these two, they've just agreed to keep it to themselves...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Mm, yes... I think I have the beginnings of a plot...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Oh, and please take these. Thanks for your help! Now, to think... perchance, to write...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hey, this is great... Now I can say I've experienced an epic battle firsthand!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought you just wanted to watch from a distance?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Well, yes, that was the original idea. But then the adventurers I was counting on didn't show up...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I noticed the monsters were slowly starting to make a move. If they'd all left, this would have been a wasted trip.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: So... I threw a stone at them. That's how the stories always go, isn't it? Throw a stone, get their attention. Or something.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: How was I to know the stone would hit one of them square on the head? And then... Well, you know the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Anyway, all's well that ends well. Sure, I got some scrapes and bruises... but boy, did I get a story too. And that's what I came for.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Finally, I can feel the creative juices starting to flow! Oh — by the way, take this for your trouble. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Methinks my writer's block has been dealt a fatal blow! I must away, my pen and paper eagerly await my return...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I just don't know where to start...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you up to now?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you again. I'm writing a new novel — well, trying to. I just can't seem to find a compelling idea for an intro.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I've been racking my brains for ages, but I'm at a complete loss. At this rate, who knows when I'll be able to start writing in earnest...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: You're a traveler, yes? You know what the world is like. So tell me, what do you think the key ingredient is to a successful novel?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Now I think about it... do you know a Sisi, by any chance? She often hangs around the harbor, waiting for some sailor named Chaoxi.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: She seems to go out and look for him on quite a regular basis. There must be a backstory there, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Do a little investigating, anyway. If you come across any good stories, note them down and bring them back here.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Ah yes, there's three children who are always playing down by the harbor. Meng, Lulu, Fei. Ring any bells?

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I know they're only children, but... between the three of them, they must have some tales to tell, surely.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Go and look into it, anyway. Make a note of any good material, and bring it back here.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Romance... I'd have my work cut out, that's for sure. My knowledge of romance is... let's say, broad strokes at the most...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: But you have a point — there are plenty of people like me in the world who are completely lacking in experience or understanding of romance. The market is ripe for the taking.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: But how would I research for a romantic story? Let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Well, how'd it go? Got a story for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here are our notes.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Ah, wonderful! Let me see... Hmm, something's not right with this Chaoxi chap... Wait, no, I take it back. Something's wrong with both of them.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Does this count as romance? Hmm... Well, romance or not, there's a plot here, at least. I can work with this.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Oh, and please take these. Thanks for bringing me some material. Now, I need to think about where to go with this story...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Hmm, I think it should work fine for a novel, although I shudder to think about how the real-life version of the story will end! Probably with the Millelith picking up the pieces...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: These two are headed for disaster...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Well, how'd it go? Got a story for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here are our notes.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Fabulous! ...But a little lacking in grit. They are only children, after all... Maybe if you went back in a few years, there'd be more of a blossoming romance there.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: I'll hold onto it, though. There's the beginnings of a story in there. It may not be bursting with romantic potential, but I can probably think of a way to flesh it out.

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Oh, and please take these. Thanks for bringing me some material. Now, I need to think about how to develop it...

dialogues.speaker: Chang the Ninth
dialogues.text: Romantic thoughts, Chang, romantic thoughts... Hmm, this is really not my forte...
